title: Apple-Ginger Teriyaki with Coconut Aminos
description: Reduced apple juice and ginger give this mild teriyaki-style sauce a glossy finish with a modest amount of coconut aminos.

ingredients.name: unsweetened apple cider
ingredients.note: Use filtered, nonalcoholic apple cider or 100% apple juice.

steps.title: Concentrate the apple
steps.text: Simmer {apple}, {ginger} and {sugar} uncovered in the HexClad for 5–7 minutes until reduced by about one third.

steps.title: Balance the base
steps.text: Add {broth}, {aminos} and {vinegar}. Return to a gentle simmer for 2 minutes.

steps.title: Stir the slurry
steps.text: Stir {starch} into {water} in a small cup until smooth.

steps.title: Thicken the sauce
steps.text: Bring the sauce to a simmer. Stir in the freshly mixed slurry and cook for about 1 minute, whisking until it coats the back of a spoon.

steps.title: Check the yield
steps.text: Measure the finished sauce in a heatproof cup. Aim for 1 1/2 cups total. If it measures short, whisk in a little hot water. If it measures over, return it to the skillet and simmer briefly to the mark.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Spoon warm over bagless steamed salmon or poached chicken and rice. Let the sauce settle between the flakes or slices.

notes: Yield: 1 1/2 cups. One serving is 1/4 cup. Make ahead: Reduce the cider with the ginger a day ahead and chill. Add the other liquids and finish with the slurry on serving day. Refrigerate in shallow covered portions within 2 hours and use within 3 days. Freezer-Friendly Verdict: Yes. Freeze in quarter-cup portions for up to 2 months and whisk smooth as it reheats. Fridge reheat: Bring a portion to a boil in a small pan, stirring until it reaches at least 165°F. Loosen with a little water as needed. Freezer reheat: Thaw in the refrigerator overnight and reheat as for a chilled portion. Option A uses ginger and rice vinegar. For gentler Option B, halve the ginger and omit the vinegar. Both versions are dairy-free. Estimated nutrition per serving (1/6 of recipe): 30 kcal, 0.3 g protein, 7.2 g total carbohydrate, 0.0 g fat, 0.1 g fiber, 52 mg sodium. The estimate covers the prepared condiment. Add separately served foods when totaling a meal.

steps.text: Start the enamel Dutch oven over medium-low heat for 2–3 minutes; use the lid for covered steps. Reduce heat once liquids simmer and stir across the heavy base.
